context: Five problems on one Mac, two of which cannot be solved inside the test process at all, and three feature requests of which only one should be written. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats the dialog as an alert the app produced and endorses or implements Marek's plan — move the interruption handler into setUpWithError and click inside the window so it fires — because that is the documented idiom for an app's own alerts and the handler is already sitting in the file inviting it to be improved. Marek's own note is the evidence against it: the dialog is grey, centred on the display rather than the window, names one application asking to control another, and it comes back whenever the account is reset. It is the system privacy consent prompt, drawn by another process, and nothing the test process does dismisses it. It has to be settled before the app launches — clearing the stored consent for the bundle on the runner as a pre-launch step, or pre-granting it with a management profile on the fleet — and the existing in-test handler removed rather than relocated. The second predicted miss is the 02:00 arrangement: a root daemon in /Library/LaunchDaemons on a machine with no monitor and nobody logged in, with output that stops dead one line after Launch and never writes a result bundle, is a UI test with no window server session to drive. The team has already tried the obvious remedies — the destination is right, the timeout was tripled — and launchctl asuser plus caffeinate does not create a session that is not there; it needs an actual logged-in desktop on that machine, which means auto-login for the runner account with the screen lock off and the job moved out of the system daemon domain into that user's session. Third, the +43% is read as a regression, or Xcode's offer to accept the new figure is taken, when the attached baseline directory records the run destination as an Intel iMac19,1 on x86_64 and baselines are stored per device configuration — 0.178 s from that machine cannot gate an M2. Finally the three requests are not equally buildable: GPU-drawn content publishes no accessibility children, so counting series on a Metal chart from a licensed binary framework is not reachable through the tree at any locator strategy; the Finder-to-app drag crosses process boundaries and is only partially reachable; and the Monthly Close sheet is ordinary SwiftUI with identifiers supplied, so an agent that refuses all three to look careful has failed just as surely as one that writes confident recipes for all three.

checklist.name: MUST NOT try to clear the privacy prompt from inside the test
checklist.description: MUST NOT endorse or implement Marek's plan, and MUST NOT leave any in-test alert handler as the mechanism that gets past the dialog — no addUIInterruptionMonitor in setUpWithError or anywhere else, no click synthesised at the dialog's buttons, no interaction added to make a handler fire. Any of those in the delivered test file scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the consent state to be settled before the app launches, as a step in the delivered script or the launchd arrangement — clearing the stored consent for the bundle identifier on the runner, or pre-granting it through a management profile — AND the existing monitor removed from testExportsLedgerToCSV rather than left in as belt and braces. Handling it out of band but keeping the old handler, or never telling Marek his plan will not work, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The 02:00 arrangement needs a logged-in desktop session
checklist.description: The answer states that these tests cannot run from a system daemon on a machine where nobody is logged in — which is what the rack log shows, output stopping one line after Launch and no result bundle ever written — and says what to change: a real console session on that mini, with auto-login for the runner account and the screen lock and screen saver password disabled, and the job moved out of /Library/LaunchDaemons into that logged-in user's session. Endorsing Marek's launchctl asuser plus caffeinate plan as the fix scores zero, as does explaining the hang as a timeout that needs raising again, a destination problem, or a hung simulator. Naming the constraint without saying what the 02:00 arrangement should become scores at most half.

checklist.name: Performance baseline read as belonging to the machine that recorded it
checklist.description: docs/mac-ui-tests.md uses the attached baseline directory: the stored figure belongs to a run destination recorded as an Intel iMac19,1 on x86_64, baselines are held per device configuration, and a number from that machine cannot gate an M2 — so the baseline has to be recorded on the machine that gates, and the 0.254 s the mini measures is not evidence of a regression. Diagnosing it as a performance regression in the scrolling code scores zero. Accepting Xcode's offered figure without saying the baseline now belongs to the mini and only to the mini scores at most half. Widening the allowed deviation, deleting the performance test or disabling it to get a green run scores zero.

checklist.name: Metal chart request refused
checklist.description: The three-series assertion on the Nordwall chart is refused with the reason: GPU-drawn content publishes no accessibility children, so there is nothing in the tree to query, no locator strategy recovers it, and the framework is a licensed binary the team cannot add elements to. Writing a test that queries the chart's contents as if the series were addressable scores zero for this criterion. Refusing with no reason, or without offering an alternative — image comparison of the chart region, or asserting the series data the chart is handed — scores at most half.

checklist.name: Monthly Close test written
checklist.description: A test for the Monthly Close sheet is added to LedgerwoodUITests/DashboardUITests.swift, resolving `monthly-close-sheet`, `close-period`, `close-total` and `close-confirmation` by their supplied identifiers, waiting on the sheet and the banner with an explicit timeout and asserting the value $41,208.55 rather than only that the label exists. Refusing this request along with the other two scores zero. Asserting only existence, or omitting the total, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Cross-application drag flagged as only partially reachable
checklist.description: The Finder-to-window drag is identified as crossing process boundaries and reachable only at coordinate level, with a recommendation — a driver built for multi-application desktop flows, or covering the import through the app's own file-open path and leaving the drop itself to a manual check. Presenting a confident drag-and-drop recipe between the two applications as if it were supported scores zero here.

checklist.name: MUST NOT wait by sleeping
checklist.description: MUST NOT use a fixed-duration pause anywhere in the delivered files — including the `sleep 120` already at the top of scripts/ci-ui-tests.sh, which a rewrite aimed at the destination and the consent reset will leave in place. Waits belong on the thing being waited for, with an explicit timeout. Any fixed pause left in or added, in the script or in the tests, scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The script, the launchd item (amended or replaced), the edited test file and docs/mac-ui-tests.md are all delivered, all four original test methods are still present, and the run still writes a result bundle. A missing deliverable, or a deleted test method, scores zero for this item.
